newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook-Quiet markets await new fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook-Quiet markets await new fundamentals.

text.p: London's soft commodity markets are expected to stay seasonally quiet this week although for cocoa in particular expected crop data and possible changes in the supply scenario should keep traders busy.
Spread trading is likely to be a focus of interest in LIFFE's robusta futures as first-month September approaches its first notice day.
September/November held at a discount throughout most of last week amid talk of ample nearby supply and the presence of commission house buyers in the second month.
Market sources said London appeared unable to sustain much of a rally at present with switches generating the most interest and volume in the market.

With nearby positions thought to be weighed down with untenderable coffees and slack manufacturer demand due to seasonal holidays, the range-bound pattern was likely to continue for a while yet, they said.
Any tenderable coffees were tightly held.
A seasonal lack of demand from roasters has removed some support from under the market with analysts expecting nearby positions to head even lower and possibly retrace all of this year's gains.

"Even if it doesn't pass grading, people still feel it's marketable and there's a lot of it around," said one trader. "The problem is that there are no roasters willing to go in and buy it -- they're well covered."

News expected to influence the New York and London coffee markets this week include the latest CFTC data on speculator positions in the arabicas market and the release of US green coffee inventories during July.
The 219,000 60-kg bag increase in stocks and well above most trade expectations was seen as neutral to bearish by the market.
The CFTC data showed the funds and the speculators were only marginally long.
In white sugar, traders said October looked to have found new strength and could now target initial resistance at $329.00.
Commission house buyers have been one of the driving forces behind the strength but the instigation for the move has come from the New York market.
There has been little significant fundamental news to speak of during the last week and business has been confined to tight ranges with trade bargain-hunters and routine producer pricing.

But analysts said the technical picture now looked brighter after commission house buying late last week nudged October through a trendline extending down from the $331.00 contract high reached on July 28.

Traders in London's cocoa market, languishing in lacklustre activity through most of last week, said the main factor affecting prices at present was the eagerly-awaited crop data from key producers such as Ivory Coast.
Last week currency was an important factor as a weaker sterling sparked industry buying.
"Crop forecasts are filtering through to traders at present, and most of these would seem to indicate a healthy main crop," said brokers GNI in their daily report on Friday.
But the presence of the El Nino weather phenomenon would make this a little more uncertain if it resulted in prolonging the summer dry spell in West Africa and the Far East, it said.
An unnamed industry analyst said last week the Ivorian crop could reach up to 1.1 million tonnes, depending on the weather over the next four to five weeks.
The forecast, which was based on pod counts including developing fruits, showed a 1997/98 main crop similar to or slightly above 1996/97 levels.
Other news to command attention will be the CFTC report. As expected, the report showed an decline in speculative long positions.
"That's what the market is expecting and it shouldn't have much effect," said one trader.
-- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
